serial_log: Serial log (written by hand on 2026-10-29 from the operator's picocom log, which is outside the repository and is not retained): the operator's session, `picocom -b 115200 /dev/ttyUSB0 --logfile <home>/src/spacemit-k3/logs/boot-7.log` on the workstation `l1`, had been running since before the M1 campaigns, and automation read the log output-only and never wrote to the serial port. The segment of this campaign, `20261029-com260-rc`, begins with the board's reboot from a one-shot boot of another project's kernel (`7.3.0-k3-kvm-csr1`, booted at 08:24 UTC; the GRUB default unchanged) into the recorded `7.3.0-65.1.riscv64.omni.fc45.riscv64` on the `k3ctl reset` made before the campaign at 17:06:55 UTC (the kernel banner at log line 110,212), on the responsible human's confirmation that the board was free and before any board command, and runs to the end of the log as read (line 128,342, the login prompt after the eleventh run's reset, 17:36 UTC). That first boot's banner reads `Web console: https://localhost:9090/` alone, the address joining later (`NetworkManager-wait-online.service` ran long, as in the M2 campaign's first reboot), and the board answered over SSH with its new boot ID before the preflight (17:08 UTC); the preflight and the two `two-guests` load checks (17:12 and 17:13 UTC) left Fedora running and show no monitor line. For each of the eleven runs the segment holds Fedora's shutdown through `systemd-kexec.service`, the kexec handoff (`kexec_core: Starting new kernel`, first at line 111,604, 17:15 UTC), the shim line, and the monitor's lines through the run's terminal marker: `BE_MVP:14 SHUTDOWN type=0 reason=0` eight times (`two-guests`, three GCC and one Clang, each with `exits_g0=157 exits_g1=157 records=138 alternations=125`; `te-poc`, three GCC and one Clang, each with both `MVPINIT 07 CHANNEL` lines, the three `BE_MVP:DENY` lines (`unmapped cause=0x15 injected=0x5 gpa=0x84001000`, `read-only cause=0x17 injected=0x7 gpa=0x84000ff8`, and the reader's second), and `exits_g0=163 exits_g1=167 denials_g0=1 denials_g1=2 records=146 alternations=127`), `BE_MVP:FAIL payload` once (before any hart started), `BE_MVP:FAIL gstage` once (`reader-write`, with its `DETAIL channel=0 domain=1 hart=2 walked=… declared=…` line, no domain run), and `BE_MVP:FAIL guest-page-fault` once (`no-inject`, after 54 lines from each guest, hart 0's one `FAIL` and `DETAIL` pair). After each terminal marker the tool's `k3ctl reset` follows (`reset_reply=OK` eleven times): the boot ROM's terse lines, `U-Boot SPL 2022.10 (May 21 2026 - 07:43:32 +0000)` with its DDR line, `U-Boot 2022.10 (May 21 2026 - 07:43:32 +0000), Build: jenkins-BSP-build-bsp-deb-395` with its device probes, `Starting kernel ...`, and Fedora Linux 45 (Server) with kernel `7.3.0-65.1.riscv64.omni.fc45.riscv64` to its login prompt, each with the board's address in its `Web console` banner; the tool saw the new boot ID in 33 to 47 s each time (33, 33, 33, 33, 33, 42, 43, 43, 43, 45, 47 s). The segment holds twelve such reboots, each legible and complete, for the pre-campaign reset and the eleven runs; no reset was made by hand, no run needed the extra reset the plan allows, and nothing was typed at the console. No line with `OpenSBI`, `Platform Name`, `Domain0`, `PMP`, `Firmware Base`, or `Runtime SBI` appears in the segment, as in M0's, M1's, and M2's campaigns (mvp/README.md open item 40): the firmware is identified only by Fedora's log, `SBI implementation ID=0x1 Version=0x10006`, which the preflight records.
